title: NECO Financial Accounting Part 1: Foundations, Final Accounts & Records - Financial Accounting - Cost classification in Manufacturing Accounts
exam: NECO Financial Accounting Part 1: Foundations, Final Accounts & Records
subject: Financial Accounting

questions.q: In a manufacturing account, which of the following best defines the formula for calculating **Prime Cost**?
options: Cost of raw materials consumed + Direct labour + Factory overheads
Cost of raw materials consumed + Direct labour + Direct expenses
Total purchases of raw materials + Direct labour + Direct expenses
Prime Cost + Factory overheads + Opening work-in-progress
questions.explain:
**Prime Cost** represents the total of all direct costs incurred in the manufacturing process. It is the sum of:
1. Direct Materials (Cost of raw materials consumed)
2. Direct Labour (e.g., manufacturing wages)
3. Direct Expenses (e.g., royalties based on units produced)

*Factory overheads* are indirect costs and are added *after* the Prime Cost to get the total factory cost.
questions.exam: NECO Financial Accounting Part 1: Foundations, Final Accounts & Records
questions.subject: Financial Accounting

questions.q: All the following expenses are correctly classified as **factory overheads** (indirect manufacturing costs) EXCEPT
options: Wages of factory supervisors and cleaners
Royalties paid per unit of goods produced
questions.explain:
**Factory overheads** are indirect costs that cannot be traced directly to a specific unit of production (e.g., depreciation, supervisory salaries, factory power). 

**Royalties** paid per unit produced are traceable directly to the units of production, classifying them as a **Direct Expense**. Therefore, royalties form part of the *Prime Cost*, not factory overheads.
